answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because velvet only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, gale is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any dune approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
